handoff.lastActionSummary: Iteration 19 completed Browser Perception: request-scoped PreparedBrowserViewContext, ensureFreshContext, extension observe_now ack/result/timeout/cancel flow, mutation quietness stabilization, prompt/direct Browser Action integration, focused smokes, dogfood evidence, project report refresh, and checkpoint.
openIssues: Semantic Interface v1 is complete for Browser Action and Vision Context conformance; Terminal/Workspace/Screen/OCR/UIA adapters are future consumers beyond iter-16.

Dedicated ranked-choice clarification card UX can still be refined; current behavior records unresolved cases, uses existing Browser Action clarification/approval surfaces, and keeps side-effect safety feature-owned.
Manual live-site Browser Action verification should be repeated after reloading the installed unpacked Browser Bridge extension so the service worker receives the latest command/status changes.
Semantic Memory uses Node's experimental built-in SQLite module and may print ExperimentalWarning during dogfood scripts.
Semantic Interface statistical calibration is deferred until a held-out dogfood trace set exists; v1 uses operating profiles plus top-vs-runner-up margin.
Codex app-server protocol remains experimental; stale persisted thread ids fall back safely, but live cross-process resume behavior needs dogfooding validation.
Browser store account submission is deferred until after dogfooding.

Vision recording/screen streaming has consent, retention, history, cleanup, skipped-frame diagnostics, resource guardrails, and Vision Context capsule preprocessing; longer CPU/memory tuning remains dogfood-dependent.
Vision Context real local ASR production backend remains behind the transcription sidecar interface until dogfooding chooses the first installed model/runtime.
Mascot motion must be reworked with real authored pose/expression/state animation assets; generated static-pose sprites are not accepted.

Browser Action native desktop executable browser chrome control is BLOCKED on a scoped Windows UI Automation or bounded native input helper; current adapter reports browser-window diagnostics, attempted PowerShell enumeration, required helper scope, and unsupported-action errors.

Browser Action custom Codex app-server tool bridge is BLOCKED on a stable app-server custom tool/client-tool contract; current coverage uses daemon prompt/tool simulation, protocol events, approval, audit, and widget-context visibility.
Restricted browser pages remain subject to browser/extension/CDP security boundaries and should report unsupported state rather than bypassing protections.
Browser Bridge uses explicit site permission for automatic page context sharing; users must enable each site or opt into broader origin permissions through extension settings.
The installed unpacked Browser Bridge extension must be reloaded after service-worker changes before the live browser uses the HTTP-first auto-observe transport.
The installed unpacked Browser Bridge extension must be reloaded after Browser Perception extension changes before live browser testing uses observe_now ack/result handling.
A broader continuous multi-tab Browser Perception scheduler can still be expanded later; iter-19 completes the request-scoped active-tab foundation required by Browser Action.
